title: Close resources in order
description:
Write a small resource tracker with to-be-closed variables:

- `Resource(name, log)` returns a table with a `name` and a metatable whose `__close` appends `"close <name>"` to `log` (a list) and sets the table's `closed` field to `true`. Creating it appends `"open <name>"`.
- `use_all(names, log, fail_at)` opens a resource for each name, **each in its own `<close>` local inside nested calls or a recursive helper**, so they are closed in reverse order when the function ends. After opening all of them it appends `"work"`. If `fail_at` is a number, opening the resource at that position (1-based) raises an error instead, after the earlier ones were opened. `use_all` itself catches nothing: the caller uses `pcall`.

```lua
local log = {}
use_all({ "db", "file", "socket" }, log)
-- log: open db, open file, open socket, work, close socket, close file, close db
```

solution.solution.lua:
local closer = {
    __close = function(r)
        table.insert(r.log, "close " .. r.name)
        r.closed = true
    end,
}

function Resource(name, log)
    table.insert(log, "open " .. name)
    return setmetatable({ name = name, log = log, closed = false }, closer)
end

local function open_from(names, i, log, fail_at)
    if i > #names then
        table.insert(log, "work")
        return
    end
    if fail_at == i then
        error("cannot open " .. names[i])
    end
    local r <close> = Resource(names[i], log)
    open_from(names, i + 1, log, fail_at)
end

function use_all(names, log, fail_at)
    open_from(names, 1, log, fail_at)
end

hints: A `<close>` local is closed when **its** block ends. To hold a variable number of them, open one per call of a recursive helper: each call's local closes when that call returns, which gives reverse order automatically.
Keep `log` inside each resource table, so one shared metatable with a single `__close` function can find where to write.
unitTests:
test("closes in reverse order", function()
    local log = {}
    use_all({ "db", "file", "socket" }, log)
    check_eq(log, { "open db", "open file", "open socket", "work", "close socket", "close file", "close db" })
end)

test("closes what was opened when something fails", function()
    local log = {}
    local ok, err = pcall(use_all, { "db", "file", "socket" }, log, 3)
    check_eq(ok, false)
    check(tostring(err):find("cannot open socket") ~= nil)
    check_eq(log, { "open db", "open file", "close file", "close db" })
end)

test("a resource on its own", function()
    local log = {}
    local r
    do
        local x <close> = Resource("solo", log)
        r = x
        check_eq(r.closed, false)
    end
    check_eq(r.closed, true)
    check_eq(log, { "open solo", "close solo" })
end)
